Grade: PP1

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PRINT AWARENESS
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Print awareness helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PRINT AWARENESS
Study Print awareness like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Print awareness”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a

What this means
In this part you learn to Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Print awareness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Print awareness”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Print awareness to a partner. (skill: Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Print awareness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’.
3. Practise this skill: Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Print awareness from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Print awareness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Print awareness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What pictures do you awareness learner should be able to: pictures and encouraged to talk about enjoy looking at?
2. What pictures interest of school. • Learners could answer questions about learners?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Print awareness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Demonstrate awareness of pictures. print in and out of school. • Learners could be engaged in ‘read aloud’.
5. Be able to: Show interest in reading in and activities. out of school. • Learners could view pictures depicting a.
